title: Partner Co-Marketing Kit — Production Economics Benchmark Report (Latency/$) — v1
content:
Last updated: 2025-02-20 (Ben)

Purpose
This kit makes it easy for marketplaces and integration partners to co-announce Redwood Inference’s public “Production Economics” benchmark report focused on latency per dollar (latency/$). It includes:
- Approved summary + partner-safe messaging
- Approved blurbs (short/medium/long)
- Co-branded slide placeholders (copy + structure)
- Coordination checklist (timing, approvals, UTMs, distribution)

Who this is for
- Cloud marketplace partners (AWS/Azure/GCP marketplace, regional cloud resellers)
- Observability/integration partners (OpenTelemetry ecosystem, LLM gateway providers, prompt/eval tool vendors)
- SI/channel partners running joint webinars or field enablement

Core principle (must-follow)
We are positioning this as a reproducible benchmark focused on production economics. We do not claim absolute superiority without context. Partners should not rewrite results or add “#1” style claims. Use approved language below.


1) What we’re launching (partner-safe summary)
Redwood Inference is publishing a public benchmark report on “production economics”: latency per dollar (latency/$), plus supporting throughput and cost metrics. Results are broken down by model family and cloud region, and backed by a published methodology with variance/limitations.

Why it matters:
Engineering teams evaluating LLM inference need a practical way to compare options beyond “best model” or “lowest cost.” Latency and cost trade off in production; latency/$ is an intuitive measure for engineering and procurement to discuss performance efficiency.

Audience:
- ML/infra engineers choosing serving infrastructure
- Platform teams standardizing inference
- Engineering leaders and procurement comparing costs across regions

What partners can say:
- “Redwood published a public benchmark report”
- “The report focuses on latency/$ and regional breakdowns”
- “Methodology and limitations are documented”

What partners should not say:
- “Redwood is the fastest/cheapest overall” (unqualified)
- “Guaranteed results for your workload”
- Any competitor callouts unless Redwood has explicitly approved the exact phrasing (not included in this kit)


2) Approved messaging blocks (copy/paste)

A) One-liner (very short)
“Redwood Inference released a production economics benchmark report measuring latency per dollar (latency/$) across popular open models and cloud regions.”

B) Short blurb (40–60 words)
“Redwood Inference published a public benchmark report focused on production economics: latency per dollar (latency/$), along with throughput and cost metrics. The report breaks results down by model family and cloud region, and includes a methodology appendix and variance guidance to help teams interpret the data.”

C) Medium blurb (90–130 words)
“Choosing an LLM inference stack in production is a balance of latency, cost, and reliability—especially across regions. Redwood Inference released a public benchmark report on ‘production economics’ that measures latency per dollar (latency/$) for common workloads and summarizes supporting metrics like p50/p95 latency and throughput. Results are reported by model family and cloud region, with published methodology and guidance on interpreting variance. The goal is to provide a credible, engineer-friendly reference for teams evaluating inference options and optimizing unit economics.”

D) Long blurb (180–240 words)
“Redwood Inference is publishing a new public benchmark report focused on production economics for LLM inference. Instead of looking at latency or cost in isolation, the report introduces latency per dollar (latency/$) as a practical way to evaluate performance efficiency for real production systems. It includes a curated set of popular open models, reports results by cloud region, and provides supporting measurements such as p50/p95 latency and throughput so readers can understand the underlying tradeoffs.

The report is designed to be credible and reproducible: it includes a methodology appendix, notes on caching/batching policies, and guidance on interpreting run-to-run variance. The intent is not to make one-size-fits-all claims, but to provide an engineer-friendly starting point for teams that need predictable inference economics across hosted, dedicated, and private deployment options.”

E) Marketplace listing “What’s new” (1–2 sentences)
“New: Redwood’s public Production Economics Benchmark Report is now available, covering latency/$ across model families and regions with a published methodology.”

F) Boilerplate (use only if needed)
“Redwood Inference is a developer-first platform for running and optimizing LLM inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.”


3) Approved CTA language
Pick 1–2 CTAs. Do not stack more than two in a single post.
- “Read the benchmark report”
- “View methodology + limitations”
- “Try it in the Redwood API”
- “Book a production economics consult” (Sales-assisted; use only for enterprise-facing partner channels)

If you need a “neutral” CTA for partner channels:
- “Explore the report and regional tables”


4) Partner social templates (with placeholders)

Notes:
- Replace [PARTNER] with partner name.
- Replace [LINK_UTM] with the UTM link provided in Section 6.
- Do not add competitor comparisons.

LinkedIn (short)
“New benchmark report from Redwood Inference: latency per dollar (latency/$) across popular open models and regions, with published methodology + variance guidance. Helpful reference for teams optimizing production inference economics. [LINK_UTM]”

LinkedIn (partner angle)
“Teams ask us how to evaluate inference options beyond cost or raw latency. Redwood Inference just published a Production Economics benchmark report focused on latency per dollar (latency/$), with regional breakdowns and methodology notes. Worth a read if you’re running LLMs in production. [LINK_UTM]”

X (short)
“Redwood Inference published a ‘production economics’ benchmark report: latency/$ + regional breakdowns + methodology. [LINK_UTM]”

X (thread opener)
“Measuring LLM inference in production means balancing latency and cost. Redwood published a benchmark report focused on latency/$ (by model + region), plus methodology and variance guidance. [LINK_UTM]”


5) Co-branded slide placeholders (copy + structure)
These are placeholders for a 5-slide partner deck. Design team can adapt to your template; keep the copy and disclosures intact.

Slide 1 — Title
Title: “Production Economics Benchmark: Latency per Dollar (latency/$)”
Subtitle: “Joint perspective: [PARTNER] x Redwood Inference”
Footer: “Public benchmark report + methodology”
Logos: [PARTNER LOGO] | [REDWOOD LOGO]

Slide 2 — Why production economics
Header: “Why latency/$?”
Bullets:
- Latency and cost trade off in production; optimizing one alone is misleading
- Regional capacity and routing policies materially impact outcomes
- Teams need a repeatable way to compare serving configurations
Disclosure (small text): “Results depend on workload and configuration; see methodology for constraints and variance guidance.”

Slide 3 — What the report covers
Header: “What’s included”
Bullets:
- Curated set of popular open models (by family)
- Results reported by cloud region
- Supporting metrics: p50/p95 latency, throughput, cost
- Methodology appendix (workloads, distributions, measurement windows)

Slide 4 — How to use the report (partner integration angle)
Header: “How teams use this in practice”
Bullets (choose 2–4):
- Establish a baseline for region selection and capacity planning
- Identify candidate models/configurations, then validate with your own prompts
- Track regression risk (variance, confidence bands) when changing configs
- Pair with [PARTNER] tooling to monitor production latency/cost and catch drift

Slide 5 — CTA + links
Header: “Get the report + methodology”
Buttons/links:
- “Read the report” → [LINK_UTM]
- “Book a consult” → [OPTIONAL_ENTERPRISE_LINK_UTM]
Footer small text: “No customer-identifying logs are published. See methodology for details.”


6) UTM + link guidance (do this every time)
Owner: Tyler Benson (Marketing Ops)

Rules:
- Every partner link must include UTM parameters.
- Use the dedicated partner UTM link we generate for you; do not copy the generic website link.
- If you need two CTAs (report + consult), we will provide two separate UTM links.

Partner UTM input we need from you:
- Partner name (exact)
- Channel type (marketplace / integration / SI / community)
- Destination (landing page / methodology appendix / consult form)
- Launch date/time + timezone

Example structure (do not self-generate; we will provide final):
https://redwoodinference.com/benchmarks/production-economics?utm_source=[partner]&utm_medium=co-marketing&utm_campaign=benchmark-report-2025&utm_content=[asset]


7) Coordination checklist (timeline + approvals)

A) Kickoff (T-14 to T-10 days)
- [Partner] Confirm participation (who posts, where, timing)
- [Redwood] Share final public launch date/time and any embargo details
- [Redwood] Provide partner UTM links (Tyler)
- [Partner] Provide logo files + brand guidelines (SVG/PNG, clearspace rules)

B) Copy review (T-10 to T-7 days)
- [Partner] Draft post/email/blog copy using approved blocks
- [Redwood] Review for claim safety + consistency (Soojin / Ben)
- [Redwood Legal] Only required if partner requests edits that impact claims/disclosures (Michael)

C) Asset production (T-7 to T-3 days)
- Co-branded slide/deck (optional)
- Co-branded blog thumbnail/hero (optional)
- Marketplace “What’s new” entry (if applicable)
- [Redwood] Provide 2–3 approved charts/screenshots if requested (must be Redwood-provided; no re-plotting)

D) Final go/no-go (T-2 to T-1 days)
- Confirm live URLs and tracking
- Confirm spokesperson/contacts for inbound
- Confirm support path for technical questions (Redwood SE contact below)

E) Launch day
- Partner posts go live within agreed window
- Send Redwood the live links (for amplification)
- Redwood to reshare/boost when appropriate

F) Post-launch (T+2 to T+14 days)
- Share basic performance summary (views/clicks/leads where available)
- Identify follow-up activity: webinar, workshop, integration guide, customer story


8) Inbound routing + who to contact (Redwood)
General partner coordination / scheduling:
- Noura El‑Khoury (Community/Events distribution)
- Ben Carter (Campaign owner)

Messaging/approval questions:
- Soojin Lee (Positioning & launch messaging)

Technical questions (benchmark methodology, reproductions, “why does my result differ?”):
- Markus Klein (SE readiness & technical talk track)

Legal/claims review (only when needed):
- Michael Grant (Legal review — claims/privacy)


9) Disclosures partners must include (pick the relevant one)
Short disclosure (social):
“Results vary by workload and configuration; see methodology for details.”

Long disclosure (blog/email):
“Benchmark results depend on workload, configuration, and region. Please refer to the methodology appendix for workload definitions, measurement windows, and guidance on interpreting variance.”


10) FAQ (partner-facing)

Q: Can we change the term “latency/$” to “performance per dollar”?
A: You can say “latency per dollar (latency/$)” and optionally add “performance efficiency” as a supporting phrase. Please keep the latency/$ term at least once so it matches the report.

Q: Can we include a competitor comparison chart?
A: Not in partner channels without explicit Redwood approval of the exact graphic and wording. Use the report link and the methodology framing.

Q: Can we host a copy of the PDF on our website?
A: Prefer linking to Redwood’s canonical landing page (for versioning + methodology updates). If you must host the PDF, coordinate with Ben + Tyler for the correct version and tracking.

Q: Can we request co-branded webinar support?
A: Yes. Provide preferred dates, audience, and how you’ll promote. We’ll align speakers based on availability (Marketing + SE).
